ceiling_directive: Fully instantiate the grouped probability-valued estimator and prove a matching same-class converse that closes the logarithmic gap across the transitional and sparse regimes.
improvement_directive: Solve the grouped reconstruction problem by specifying its split, shells, degree, factorial statistics, covariance control, positive moment program, normalization, and fallback, then derive its uniform squared-Wasserstein risk. Prove a matching converse on the unchanged observational class to determine the exact sparse-to-dense rate and consistency boundary.
critique: The advertised research object is the sharp all-regime frontier, but the note proves an exact rate only for n at least d cubed and leaves every transitional and sparse elbow unresolved by a logarithmic factor. The grouped reconstruction procedure is merely a blueprint, so it supplies neither the promised improved estimator nor an achievable sparse-regime rate. The scalar-transfer lower bound also imports a theorem identified only by an internal repository label, without public theorem text or a precise archival citation, and therefore requires source verification before the logarithmic bracket and necessary consistency condition are reproducible. The TL;DR and scope sections accurately disclose these limitations, but the delivered dense theorem, coarse bracket, and parametric-risk boundary constitute a companion result rather than the field-level full-frontier contribution named in the brief.
